newsitem.title: USA: Gun control advocates push for handgun lock law.
newsitem.headline: Gun control advocates push for handgun lock law.

text.p: Gun control advocates are promoting a law in Maryland that would require gun dealers to provide child safety locks on every handgun they sell.
President Clinton mentioned child safety locks in his State of the Union address to Congress last month and is expected to propose a similar regulation in a juvenile crime prevention package.

Sarah Brady, wife of former White House press secretary James Brady who was disabled in 1981 when shot during an assassination attempt on former President Ronald Reagan, is leading the Maryland campaign.

Brady, the head of Handgun Control Inc., said in a statement that "while parents must recognise the dangers of bringing guns into the home, these proposals (for locks) unabashedly demand that the gun industry start to take responsibility for the lethal products they manufacture."
Earlier this month, the Chicago City Council passed an ordinance requiring that all handguns sold there have the locks and there is a proposal in Massachusetts to do the same.
The locks would add about $10 to the cost of a gun.

In 1994, 512 unintentional deaths were recorded for people under the age of 19 involving firearms. Nearly 6,000 deaths by firearms in the same age category were reported through homicide, suicide, accident or for unknown reasons, according to the National Centre for Health Statistics.
